result:
**Not ready to publish.** Two problems.

**Claims list**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Rated 4.8 out of 5 from over 1,200 reviews on our website" | Allowlisted |
| "organic loose leaf" | Allowlisted (certified organic by the Soil Association) |
| "The finest" | **Unsupported superlative.** Nothing on the allowlist backs a "finest" claim, and it fails the "compared to what?" test. |
| "eco-friendly bags" | **Unsupported vague green claim.** The allowlist backs "plastic-free" and "home compostable", not "eco-friendly". Under UK CMA Green Claims Code rules, a broad environmental claim needs to be specific and substantiated. |
| "packed by hand in Bristol" | Allowlisted for tins. The sentence also attaches it to the bags, which the allowlist doesn't cover, so the wording is worth tightening. |

**Suggested rewrite**

> Rated 4.8 out of 5 from over 1,200 reviews on our website. Certified organic loose leaf tea from the Soil Association, plus plastic-free, home compostable tea bags. Every tin packed by hand in Bristol.

This swaps "finest" for the certified fact, replaces "eco-friendly" with the two specific claims we can back, and limits the hand-packing claim to tins. Check that the landing page itself carries the same claims, since an ad or hero line shouldn't say more than the page does.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "The finest organic loose leaf", "type": "superlative"}, {"quote": "eco-friendly bags", "type": "green_claim"}], "publish": false}
```
